records.query: Need the patient's platelet count, D-dimer, fibrinogen, anti-PF4/heparin-induced thrombocytopenia antibody assay, and CT imaging to assess thrombosis and adrenal hemorrhage—these are core tests to confirm vaccine-associated VITT/TTS and distinguish it from pulmonary embolism or splanchnic ischemia.

Need serial platelet counts with peripheral smear, D-dimer/fibrinogen values, anti-PF4 ELISA result, and contrast-enhanced CT of chest/abdomen including adrenal glands—these are essential to confirm vaccine-associated VITT/TTS by demonstrating thrombocytopenia, consumptive coagulopathy, and thrombosis/adrenal hemorrhage, and to distinguish it from pulmonary embolism and splanchnic ischemia.

Need the patient's complete blood count with platelet count, D-dimer, fibrinogen, and anti-PF4 ELISA antibody results, plus CT pulmonary angiography and contrast-enhanced abdominal CT to evaluate pulmonary embolism, splanchnic vein thrombosis, or adrenal hemorrhage—these are the core laboratory and imaging findings required to confirm or exclude VITT/TTS.

Need the functional platelet activation assay (serotonin release assay) to confirm VITT, and brain MRI/MRV to exclude cerebral venous sinus thrombosis given lethargy. These results are critical to verify the leading VITT/TTS hypothesis.

Need the actual results of the anti-PF4 ELISA and serotonin release assay, the contrast-enhanced abdominal CT report specifically detailing splanchnic vein patency and adrenal morphology, and a repeat platelet count to confirm or exclude VITT/TTS complicated by splanchnic vein thrombosis, as these are the decisive findings for the leading hypothesis.

Need blood cultures, procalcitonin, and lactate results to exclude occult sepsis as an alternative cause of fever, hypotension, and lethargy; because VITT/TTS diagnosis requires no alternative explanation, these are essential to secure the leading hypothesis of VITT/TTS complicated by splanchnic vein thrombosis.

Need the actual results of the platelet count, D-dimer, fibrinogen, anti-PF4 ELISA, and the contrast-enhanced abdominal CT findings focusing on splanchnic veins and adrenal glands—these are the core evidence to confirm or refute VITT/TTS complicated by splanchnic vein thrombosis.

Need the actual results of the previously requested core tests: platelet count, D-dimer, fibrinogen, anti-PF4 ELISA, and contrast-enhanced abdominal CT focusing on splanchnic veins and adrenal glands—these are essential to confirm or refute VITT/TTS complicated by splanchnic vein thrombosis.

Need the actual results of platelet count, D-dimer, fibrinogen, anti-PF4 ELISA, serotonin release assay, and contrast-enhanced abdominal CT focusing on splanchnic veins and adrenal glands—these are essential to confirm or exclude VITT/TTS complicated by splanchnic vein thrombosis, the current leading hypothesis.

Need the actual results of platelet count, D-dimer, fibrinogen, anti-PF4 ELISA, serotonin release assay, and contrast-enhanced abdominal CT focusing on splanchnic veins and adrenal glands—these are the core evidence required to definitively confirm or refute VITT/TTS complicated by splanchnic vein thrombosis.

Need the patient's medication administration record to confirm no recent heparin exposure, along with the exact Johnson & Johnson vaccine lot number and administration date, because confirming absence of heparin exposure and vaccine-specific details is essential to meet VITT/TTS diagnostic criteria and exclude heparin-induced thrombocytopenia.

Need the peripheral blood smear, ADAMTS13 activity, and PT/INR results to exclude alternative thrombotic microangiopathies and DIC, because VITT/TTS requires ruling out other causes of thrombocytopenia and thrombosis, and these tests have not yet been requested.

bindings.label: A 33-year-old man presented with a 1-day history of hemoptysis, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and dyspnea on exertion, and appeared lethargic on examination
Patient is a 33-year-old man with no medical history; he received the Johnson & Johnson COVID vaccination approximately 4 weeks before presentation

Initial vitals: temperature 98.9°F, heart rate 76 beats/min, blood pressure 90/55 mm Hg, SpO₂ 99% on room air; physical examination showed a lethargic man with unremarkable cardiopulmonary and abdominal examinations and no lymphadenopathy
Patient developed a low-grade fever of 100°F on day 1
Patient denied orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, sore throat, runny nose, diarrhea, urinary symptoms, night sweats, and recent tuberculosis contact
Vaccine-associated VITT/TTS
Pulmonary embolism/infarction
Acute infection/sepsis
Acute splanchnic ischemia
Expert analyses recommend contrast-enhanced CT/abdominal CT to evaluate for thrombosis and adrenal hemorrhage
VITT/TTS complicated by splanchnic vein thrombosis and/or adrenal hemorrhage
VITT/TTS complicated by splanchnic vein thrombosis
VITT/TTS complicated by pulmonary embolism/infarction
VITT/TTS complicated by adrenal hemorrhage
VITT/TTS complicated by cerebral venous sinus thrombosis
VITT/TTS with isolated thrombocytopenia/coagulopathy without detectable thrombosis
Anti-PF4 ELISA, serotonin release assay, platelet count, D-dimer, fibrinogen, and contrast-enhanced abdominal CT have been requested to evaluate VITT/TTS
Actual results of platelet count, D-dimer, fibrinogen, anti-PF4 ELISA, serotonin release assay, and contrast-enhanced abdominal CT remain unavailable despite retrieval attempts
Radiologist and laboratory physician analyses both identify VITT/TTS complicated by splanchnic vein thrombosis as the leading hypothesis
Laboratory physician reports all confirmatory results remain pending after three retrieval attempts
Radiologist notes that sepsis and thrombotic microangiopathy are not fully excluded
Patient may have thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA)
Immunofluorescence microscopy demonstrated linear IgA deposition along the basement membrane
